questions.text: What does the Italian term forte (marked f) mean?
questions.solution: Forte means loud; its sign is f, and the opposite is piano (p), meaning soft
questions.hint: Think of the opposite of piano (p)

feedback: Soft is piano (p); forte is its opposite
Fast is a tempo marking such as allegro, not a dynamic

questions.text: Which Italian term means 'gradually getting louder'?
questions.solution: Crescendo (cresc.) means gradually getting louder; its sign is an opening hairpin <
questions.hint: Its sign looks like a hairpin that opens out

feedback: Diminuendo means gradually getting softer
Rallentando means gradually getting slower
Accelerando means gradually getting faster

questions.text: Which element of music describes the speed of the music?
questions.solution: Tempo is the speed of the music, given by terms such as allegro or andante, or by a metronome mark
questions.hint: Allegro and adagio are markings for this element

feedback: Timbre is the tone colour of a sound
Dynamics describe how loud or soft the music is

questions.text: Which Italian term means 'very soft' (marked pp)? Give the term.
questions.solution: Pianissimo (pp) means very soft
questions.hint: Add the ending -issimo to the term for soft

feedback.piano: Piano (p) means soft; very soft is pianissimo (pp)

questions.text: A short musical pattern is repeated many times in a row. Give the Italian term for this device.
questions.solution: A repeated musical pattern is an ostinato (in pop music it is often called a riff)
questions.hint: The word comes from the Italian for 'stubborn' or 'obstinate'

questions.text: What does 'timbre' describe?
questions.solution: Timbre (sonority) is the tone colour that makes a trumpet sound different from a violin playing the same note
questions.hint: It is why a flute and a violin playing the same note still sound different

options: How loud or soft the music is
How many layers of sound there are
The particular sound quality or tone colour of an instrument or voice
feedback: That is dynamics
That is texture
That is tempo

questions.text: What does the Italian term staccato mean?
questions.solution: Staccato notes are short and detached, shown by a dot above or below the note
questions.hint: It is shown by a small dot above or below the note head

feedback: Smooth and connected playing is legato

questions.text: Which tempo marking is the slowest?
questions.solution: Largo means very slow and broad; andante is a walking pace, moderato is moderate and allegro is fast
questions.hint: Put the terms in order: walking pace, moderate, fast… which is left?

feedback: Andante is at a walking pace, faster than largo
Allegro means fast and lively
Moderato means at a moderate speed

questions.text: Which dynamic marking is quieter than mezzo piano (mp)?
questions.solution: From quiet to loud: pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff; so piano (p) is quieter than mezzo piano
questions.hint: Mezzo means 'moderately', so mezzo piano is a little louder than the plain marking

feedback: Mezzo forte is moderately loud, so it is louder than mp

questions.text: Which statement about legato and staccato is accurate?
questions.solution: Legato means smooth and connected (often shown by a slur); staccato means short and detached (a dot)
questions.hint: These terms describe articulation, not volume or speed

options: Legato is short and detached; staccato is smooth and connected
Legato is loud; staccato is soft
Legato is fast; staccato is slow
Legato is smooth and connected; staccato is short and detached
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which Italian term means 'gradually getting slower'? Give the term.
questions.solution: Rallentando (rall.) or ritardando (rit.) means gradually getting slower
questions.hint: It is the opposite of accelerando

questions.text: Which texture has all the parts moving together in the same rhythm, like a hymn?
questions.solution: Homophonic (chordal) texture has the parts moving together in chords, as in most hymns
questions.hint: 'Homo' means 'same': the parts share the same rhythm

feedback: Monophonic is a single melody line with no accompaniment
Polyphonic has several independent melodies at once

questions.text: Which cadence is made of chord V followed by chord I?
questions.solution: A perfect cadence is V–I and sounds finished
questions.hint: This cadence is used at the end of most pieces because it sounds complete

feedback: A plagal cadence is IV–I
An imperfect cadence ends on chord V
An interrupted cadence is usually V–VI

questions.text: Name the texture made of a single melody line with no accompaniment. Give the term.
questions.solution: A single unaccompanied melody line is a monophonic texture
questions.hint: 'Mono' means one

feedback.homophonic: Homophonic means parts moving together in chords
feedback.polyphonic: Polyphonic means several independent melodies at once

questions.text: A piece is marked Allegro. How should it be played?
questions.solution: Allegro means fast and lively
questions.hint: It is a tempo marking often used for the first movement of a symphony

feedback: At a walking pace is andante
That is rallentando

questions.text: A bass part plays the same four-note pattern over and over while the melody changes above it. Which device is this?
questions.solution: A short pattern repeated over and over is an ostinato; a repeating bass pattern like this is also called a ground bass
questions.hint: The pattern repeats again and again without changing

feedback: A sequence repeats a phrase at a higher or lower pitch
Imitation is when another part copies a melody
A pedal is a single sustained or repeated note

questions.text: A melodic phrase is repeated straight away but starting one note higher. Which device is this?
questions.solution: Repeating a phrase at a higher or lower pitch is a sequence
questions.hint: The phrase keeps its shape but moves up in pitch

feedback: An ostinato repeats at the same pitch
A drone is a held note or notes

questions.text: In a rhythm, the accents fall on weak beats and off-beats instead of the strong beats. What is this called?
questions.solution: Accenting weak beats or off-beats is syncopation
questions.hint: It gives an 'off-beat' feel that is common in jazz and pop

feedback: Rubato is flexible tempo
Augmentation makes note values longer

questions.text: Folk music has two notes, the tonic and the dominant, held throughout like the bagpipes. Give the one-word term.
questions.solution: Held notes, often the tonic and dominant as on bagpipes, form a drone
questions.hint: Think of the low, steady sound of the bagpipes under the tune

questions.text: A single note is marked sfz to show a sudden, strong accent. Give the full Italian term.
questions.solution: sfz stands for sforzando (or sforzato): a sudden strong accent
questions.hint: The Italian word begins with the letters s and f

questions.text: A song's sections run verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus. Which element of music does this describe?
questions.solution: The order of sections in a piece is its structure (or form)
questions.hint: This element is about how a piece is organised into sections

feedback: Texture is about the layers of sound
Harmony is about chords

questions.text: A passage starts at pp and ends at ff over eight bars. Which description is accurate?
questions.solution: pp is pianissimo (very soft) and ff is fortissimo (very loud), so the music gets gradually louder: a crescendo
questions.hint: First decode pp and ff, then decide whether the music gets louder or softer

options: A diminuendo from very loud to very soft
A crescendo from soft to moderately loud
An accelerando from slow to fast
A crescendo from very soft to very loud
feedback: pp comes first, so the music gets louder, not softer
pp and ff are dynamics, not tempo markings

questions.text: Bars 1–4 are marked Andante, bar 5 is marked accel. and bar 9 is marked a tempo. What happens to the speed?
questions.solution: accel. (accelerando) means gradually faster; a tempo means go back to the original speed
questions.hint: Decode accel. first, then think about what 'a tempo' tells the player

options: It gets gradually faster from bar 5, then returns to the original speed at bar 9
It gets gradually slower from bar 5, then returns to the original speed at bar 9
It suddenly becomes very fast at bar 5 and stays fast
It gets gradually faster from bar 5 and keeps getting faster after bar 9
feedback: Gradually slower would be rall. or rit.; accel. means gradually faster

questions.text: The sections of a piece are A B A C A D A. Give the name of this structure.
questions.solution: A main theme (A) that keeps returning between different episodes is rondo form
questions.hint: Notice which section keeps coming back between the others

feedback.ternary: Ternary form is A B A

questions.text: A phrase ends with chord IV followed by chord I. Which cadence is this?
questions.solution: IV–I is a plagal cadence, often sung to 'Amen' at the end of hymns
questions.hint: Look at the first chord: is it V or IV?

options: Perfect, often called the Amen cadence
Plagal, often called the Amen cadence
feedback: A perfect cadence is V–I, not IV–I

questions.text: A phrase ends on chord V, so the music sounds unfinished, as if it is asking a question. Which cadence is this?
questions.solution: A cadence that ends on chord V is imperfect and sounds unfinished
questions.hint: Which cadence ends on the dominant chord rather than the tonic?

feedback: A perfect cadence ends on chord I and sounds finished
An interrupted cadence goes from V to a surprise chord, usually VI

questions.text: In C major, a phrase ends with chord V (G major) followed by chord VI (A minor) instead of chord I. Which cadence is this?
questions.solution: V–VI is an interrupted cadence: the ear expects chord I but hears a surprise chord
questions.hint: The ear expects V–I, but something else happens

feedback: A perfect cadence would be V–I
An imperfect cadence ends on chord V

questions.text: A piece has the structure A B A, where the return of A matches the opening. Give the name of this structure.
questions.solution: A B A is ternary form (three parts, with the opening section returning)
questions.hint: 'Ter' means three

feedback.binary: Binary form has only two sections, A B
feedback.rondo: Rondo is A B A C A…

questions.text: Which statement about a polyphonic texture is accurate?
questions.solution: Polyphonic (contrapuntal) texture has several independent melodic lines at once, as in a fugue
questions.hint: 'Poly' means many

options: Two or more independent melodies are heard at the same time
One melody is played with no accompaniment
All the parts play the same melody in octaves
A melody is accompanied by sustained chords that move together
feedback: That is a monophonic texture
That is playing in octaves, not polyphony

questions.text: Which harmonic feature is most likely to make music sound tense and unsettled?
questions.solution: Dissonance (notes that clash) creates tension; consonant chords and perfect cadences sound stable
questions.hint: Think about which chords sound 'clashing' rather than restful

options: A perfect cadence at the end of each phrase
Simple chords I, IV and V only
feedback: A perfect cadence sounds finished and restful

questions.text: Which statement about rubato is accurate?
questions.solution: Rubato ('robbed time') means pushing and pulling the tempo for expression, common in Romantic piano music
questions.hint: The Italian word means 'robbed' or 'stolen' time

options: The performer keeps a strict, unchanging beat
The performer plays every note detached
The performer slightly speeds up and slows down for expression
feedback: That is staccato
That is a crescendo

questions.text: Which statement correctly compares a perfect and an imperfect cadence?
questions.solution: Perfect = V–I (finished); imperfect = any chord to V (unfinished)
questions.hint: Decide which chord each cadence ends on

options: A perfect cadence ends on chord V; an imperfect cadence ends on chord I
Both end on chord I, but an imperfect cadence is quieter
A perfect cadence is IV–I; an imperfect cadence is V–VI
A perfect cadence (V–I) sounds finished; an imperfect cadence (ending on V) sounds unfinished
feedback: That is the wrong way round
IV–I is plagal and V–VI is interrupted

questions.text: The violins play a melody, then the cellos copy it two beats later while the violins carry on. Give the one-word term for this copying device.
questions.solution: When one part copies another part's melody shortly afterwards, it is imitation (strict imitation throughout is a canon)
questions.hint: One part is copying, or 'echoing', another

questions.text: A melody in a major key suddenly uses several notes that are not in that key. How is this melody described?
questions.solution: Notes from outside the key make a melody chromatic; diatonic melodies use only the notes of the key
questions.hint: Is the melody staying inside the key or moving outside it?

feedback: Diatonic means using only the notes of the key
Conjunct describes stepwise movement, not notes outside the key

questions.text: Which note value lasts for 1 beat in 4/4 time?
questions.solution: In 4/4 the beat is a crotchet, so a crotchet lasts 1 beat
questions.hint: The bottom 4 in 4/4 means the beat is a quarter note

feedback: A minim lasts 2 beats
A quaver lasts half a beat
A semibreve lasts 4 beats

questions.text: In 4/4 time, how many crotchet beats does a minim last? Give a number.
questions.solution: A minim is worth two crotchets, so it lasts 2 beats
questions.hint: A minim is a half note

questions.text: Give the British name for the note worth 4 crotchet beats (a whole note).
questions.solution: A semibreve lasts 4 crotchet beats (a whole bar of 4/4)
questions.hint: Its name starts with 'semi' and it looks like an open oval with no stem

feedback.semiquaver: A semiquaver is a quarter of a beat

questions.text: Which clef is also called the G clef? Give the name of the clef.
questions.solution: The treble clef curls around the G line, so it is called the G clef
questions.hint: This clef is used for higher instruments such as the violin and flute

feedback.bass: The bass clef is the F clef
feedback.bass clef: The bass clef is the F clef

questions.text: What does a sharp sign (♯) do to a note?
questions.solution: A sharp raises a note by one semitone; a flat lowers it by one semitone
questions.hint: Think of the next key up on a piano

options: Cancels an earlier sharp or flat
feedback: That is a flat
That is a natural sign

questions.text: Give the British name for the note worth half a crotchet (an eighth note).
questions.solution: A quaver lasts half a crotchet beat
questions.hint: It has a filled-in head and one tail or flag

feedback.semiquaver: A semiquaver is a quarter of a crotchet

questions.text: How many lines does a music stave have?
questions.solution: A stave has five lines and four spaces
questions.hint: Count the spaces too: there are four of them

questions.text: Which time signature has three crotchet beats in each bar?
questions.solution: 3/4 has 3 crotchet beats per bar, as in a waltz
questions.hint: The top number tells you how many beats

feedback: 6/8 has six quavers in two dotted-crotchet beats

questions.text: In a simple time signature such as 3/4, what does the top number tell you?
questions.solution: The top number gives the number of beats per bar; the bottom number gives the beat's note value
questions.hint: In 3/4 the top number is 3

options: How many beats there are in each bar
Which note value is one beat
Which key the music is in
feedback: That is the bottom number

questions.text: A dot written after a note changes its length. What does the dot add?
questions.solution: A dot after a note adds half its value: a dotted minim is 2 + 1 = 3 beats
questions.hint: Try it with a minim: what is a dotted minim worth?

options: A quarter of the note's value
The same value again, doubling it
feedback: A dot above or below the note means staccato; a dot after the note lengthens it

questions.text: Which major key has one sharp, F♯, in its key signature?
questions.solution: G major has one sharp, F♯
questions.hint: The sharp is the 7th note of the scale; count up from the key note

feedback: D major has two sharps
F major has one flat, B♭
C major has no sharps or flats

questions.text: What is the interval from C up to the G above it? Give its full name (quality and number).
questions.solution: C D E F G is five letter names, and C to G is a perfect 5th
questions.hint: Count the letter names from C to G, including both

feedback.perfect fourth: C to F is a perfect 4th; count again including both C and G

questions.text: Where is middle C written in the treble clef?
questions.solution: Middle C sits on its own short ledger line just below the treble stave
questions.hint: The bottom line of the treble stave is E; go down from there

options: On the bottom line of the stave
On the middle line of the stave
In the top space of the stave
On a ledger line just below the stave
feedback: The bottom line of the treble stave is E

questions.text: How many quavers are equal to one minim? Give a number.
questions.solution: A minim is 2 crotchets and each crotchet is 2 quavers, so 2 × 2 = 4
questions.hint: First find how many crotchets are in a minim

mistakes.feedback: 2 quavers make a crotchet, not a minim

questions.text: Which sign cancels an earlier sharp or flat, returning the note to its normal pitch? Give the term.
questions.solution: A natural sign (♮) cancels a sharp or flat
questions.hint: The sign looks like a box with two stems; the note goes back to normal

questions.text: In 3/4 time, a bar already contains a minim. How many more crotchet beats are needed to complete the bar? Give a number.
questions.solution: 3/4 needs 3 beats; a minim is 2, so 3 − 2 = 1 more beat
questions.hint: How many beats does a bar of 3/4 hold?

questions.text: In the treble clef, which note sits on the bottom line of the stave?
questions.solution: Treble clef lines from the bottom are E, G, B, D, F, so the bottom line is E
questions.hint: The treble clef lines have a well-known rhyme, read from the bottom line upwards

feedback: G is the bottom line in the bass clef, or the second line in the treble clef

questions.text: In the treble clef, the four spaces from bottom to top spell a word. Give the word.
questions.solution: The treble clef spaces are F, A, C, E
questions.hint: The word is something on the front of your head

questions.text: Which major key has two sharps, F♯ and C♯?
questions.solution: D major has two sharps: F♯ and C♯
questions.hint: G major has one sharp; add the next sharp in the order of sharps

feedback: G major has only one sharp
A major has three sharps
F major has one flat

questions.text: In C major, which chord is chord V (the dominant)?
questions.solution: Count up five notes from C: C D E F G, so chord V is G major
questions.hint: Count up the scale from C to the 5th note

feedback: F major is chord IV (the subdominant)
A minor is chord VI

questions.text: Which key is the relative minor of C major?
questions.solution: A minor shares C major's key signature (no sharps or flats), so it is the relative minor
questions.hint: The relative minor starts on the 6th note of the major scale

feedback: C minor is the tonic minor; it has three flats
E minor is the relative minor of G major

questions.text: Which pair of notes lasts the same length as a dotted minim?
questions.solution: A dotted minim is 2 + 1 = 3 beats, the same as a minim (2) plus a crotchet (1)
questions.hint: First work out the dotted minim: a minim plus half a minim

feedback: Two crotchets make 2 beats, not 3
Two minims make 4 beats

questions.text: Name the scale that uses only five different notes and is common in folk music around the world. Give the term.
questions.solution: A five-note scale is a pentatonic scale
questions.hint: 'Penta' means five, as in pentagon

questions.text: A piece has one flat in its key signature and ends on a D minor chord. Which key is it most likely in?
questions.solution: One flat means F major or its relative minor, D minor; ending on a D minor chord points to D minor
questions.hint: Which major key has one flat, and what is its relative minor?

feedback: F major also has one flat, but the piece ends on D minor
B♭ major has two flats

questions.text: The major scale pattern is tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. Starting on F, which accidental is needed?
questions.solution: F to G to A are tones; A to the 4th note must be a semitone, so B becomes B♭ (B flat)
questions.hint: Work up from F step by step; the 3rd to 4th notes must be a semitone apart

feedback: F♯ is needed in G major, not F major
F major's 7th note is E natural, a semitone below F

questions.text: A bar of 4/4 contains a dotted crotchet, a quaver and a minim. How many crotchet beats is that in total? Give a number.
questions.solution: Dotted crotchet 1.5 + quaver 0.5 + minim 2 = 4 beats
questions.hint: Write the value of each note in crotchet beats, then add

mistakes.feedback: Remember the dot adds half: a dotted crotchet is 1.5 beats

questions.text: Starting on C, count up 4 semitones. Which interval is this?
questions.solution: C → C♯ → D → D♯ → E is 4 semitones, and C to E is a major 3rd
questions.hint: Count the semitones on a keyboard, including black keys

feedback: A minor 3rd is 3 semitones (C to E♭)
A perfect 4th is 5 semitones

questions.text: In the bass clef, which note is on the top line of the stave?
questions.solution: Bass clef lines from the bottom are G, B, D, F, A, so the top line is A
questions.hint: The bass clef lines have their own rhyme, starting from G on the bottom line

feedback: F is the 4th line (the line between the two dots of the bass clef)
G is the bottom line of the bass clef

questions.text: The notes C, E and G are played together. Give the name of this chord (letter name and major or minor).
questions.solution: C, E, G is the C major triad: root C, major 3rd E and perfect 5th G
questions.hint: The lowest note is the root; check whether the 3rd is major (4 semitones) or minor

feedback.C minor: C minor would have E♭, not E

questions.text: Which description of the key of A minor is accurate?
questions.solution: A minor is the relative minor of C major, so both have no sharps or flats in the key signature
questions.hint: Find the major key whose 6th note is A

options: One sharp, F♯, in its key signature
No sharps or flats in its key signature, the same as C major
Three flats in its key signature
The relative minor of G major
feedback: One sharp is G major or E minor
The relative minor of G major is E minor

questions.text: A bar of 4/4 contains a minim, a crotchet and a quaver. What is wrong with it?
questions.solution: 2 + 1 + 0.5 = 3.5 beats, so the bar needs another half beat to make 4
questions.hint: Add up the beats: minim, crotchet and quaver

options: Half a beat short: it needs another quaver or a quaver rest
Nothing is wrong: it adds up to four beats

questions.text: Which statement about tones and semitones is accurate?
questions.solution: A tone is two semitones; E–F and B–C are semitones because there is no black key between them
questions.hint: Look at a keyboard: which white keys have no black key between them?

options: A semitone is equal to two tones
E to F is a tone
Every pair of white keys next to each other is a tone apart
A tone is equal to two semitones
feedback: E to F is a semitone: there is no black key between them
E–F and B–C are only a semitone apart

questions.text: A piece in C major changes key to G major halfway through. Which description is accurate?
questions.solution: G is the 5th note (dominant) of C major, so moving to G major is a modulation to the dominant
questions.hint: Count up from C to G: which degree of the scale is G?

options: It modulates to the dominant key
It modulates to the subdominant key
It modulates to the relative minor
It stays in the tonic key
feedback: The subdominant of C is F
The relative minor of C major is A minor

questions.text: Why is 6/8 described as compound duple time?
questions.solution: 6/8 has six quavers grouped in two dotted-crotchet beats (duple), and each beat splits into three (compound)
questions.hint: Group the six quavers into beats: how many groups, and how many quavers in each?

options: It has six crotchet beats per bar
It has two dotted-crotchet beats per bar, each dividing into three quavers
It has two crotchet beats per bar, each dividing into two quavers
It has three beats per bar, each dividing into two quavers
feedback: That describes 2/4, which is simple duple
That describes 3/4

questions.text: What is the interval between two notes with the same letter name, eight notes apart, such as C to the next C up? Give the term.
questions.solution: From one note to the next note with the same letter name is an octave (8 notes)
questions.hint: 'Oct' means eight, as in octopus

questions.text: Which family of the orchestra does the trumpet belong to?
questions.solution: The trumpet is a brass instrument: the player buzzes their lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece
questions.hint: Think about how the sound is made: buzzing lips into a metal mouthpiece

questions.text: Which of these is a woodwind instrument?
questions.solution: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument played with a single reed
questions.hint: Look for the instrument that uses a reed

feedback: The trombone is brass
The cello is a string instrument
Timpani are percussion

questions.text: Which voice type is the highest female voice?
questions.solution: From high to low the main voices are soprano, alto, tenor and bass (SATB)
questions.hint: SATB lists the voices from highest to lowest

feedback: Alto is the lower female voice
Tenor is a male voice

questions.text: Give the Italian term that tells string players to pluck the strings with their fingers.
questions.solution: Pizzicato (pizz.) means plucking the strings
questions.hint: Its abbreviation is four letters long

feedback.arco: Arco means play with the bow

questions.text: Which instruments make up a standard string quartet?
questions.solution: A string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello
questions.hint: There are four players, and two of them play the same instrument

options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
Two violins, a cello and a piano
Two violins, a viola and a cello
feedback: A string quartet has two violins and no double bass

questions.text: Give the name of the lowest-pitched instrument in the orchestral string family.
questions.solution: The double bass is the largest and lowest orchestral string instrument
questions.hint: It is so big that the player stands or sits on a high stool

feedback.cello: The cello is low, but the double bass is lower

questions.text: Which of these is a tuned percussion instrument?
questions.solution: A xylophone has wooden bars tuned to definite pitches, so it is tuned percussion
questions.hint: Which one can play a melody?

feedback: A snare drum has no definite pitch
A triangle is untuned percussion

questions.text: Which of these instruments uses a double reed?
questions.solution: The oboe (like the bassoon) uses a double reed
questions.hint: Two reeds vibrate against each other; it is not a single reed on a mouthpiece

feedback: The clarinet uses a single reed
The flute uses no reed: you blow across a hole
The saxophone uses a single reed

questions.text: After a pizzicato passage, which Italian term tells string players to go back to using the bow? Give the term.
questions.solution: Arco means play with the bow again
questions.hint: It is a short four-letter word

questions.text: Which brass instrument changes pitch using a slide instead of valves?
questions.solution: The trombone uses a slide to change the length of its tube
questions.hint: The player moves part of the instrument in and out

feedback: The trumpet uses valves
The tuba uses valves

questions.text: Which voice type is the highest common adult male voice (not counting the countertenor)?
questions.solution: Male voices from high to low: (countertenor), tenor, baritone, bass
questions.hint: SATB: which male voice comes before bass?

feedback: Baritone is between tenor and bass
Mezzo-soprano is a female voice

questions.text: Which statement about the piano and the harpsichord is accurate?
questions.solution: Pressing a piano key makes a hammer strike the string; pressing a harpsichord key makes a quill pluck it
questions.hint: The piano's full name, pianoforte, shows that it can play soft and loud depending on how hard it is hit

options: Piano strings are struck by hammers; harpsichord strings are plucked
Piano strings are plucked; harpsichord strings are struck by hammers
Piano strings are bowed; harpsichord strings are struck
The harpsichord has no strings and uses pipes
feedback: That is the wrong way round
The organ uses pipes

questions.text: Which Baroque keyboard instrument plucks its strings? Give the instrument.
questions.solution: The harpsichord plucks its strings, so it cannot make gradual changes in volume
questions.hint: It often played the continuo part in Baroque music

feedback.piano: The piano hits its strings with hammers

questions.text: Which arrangement correctly orders a system as input, then process, then output?
questions.solution: A microphone picks up sound (input), the mixing desk processes it and the loudspeaker plays it (output)
questions.hint: Which device picks up the sound in the first place?

questions.text: A player blows across a hole in the side of the instrument, with no reed. Which instrument is it?
questions.solution: The flute has no reed: the player blows across the mouth hole
questions.hint: Which woodwind instrument is held sideways?

feedback: The oboe uses a double reed
The clarinet uses a single reed
The bassoon uses a double reed

questions.text: A string player moves the bow very quickly back and forth on one note to make a trembling sound. Which technique is this?
questions.solution: Rapid bowing back and forth on one note is (bowed) tremolo
questions.hint: The name comes from the Italian for 'trembling'

feedback: Vibrato is a small wobble in pitch made by the finger on the string
A glissando is a slide between pitches

questions.text: A violinist plays two strings at the same time. Which technique is this?
questions.solution: Playing two strings at once is double stopping
questions.hint: The fingers 'stop' two strings at once

feedback: Col legno means playing with the wood of the bow
Con sordino means with a mute

questions.text: A singer slides smoothly from one pitch to another. Give the term for this slide.
questions.solution: A smooth slide between pitches is a glissando (in singing it is often called portamento)
questions.hint: Think of running a finger quickly along the keys of a piano

questions.text: A producer places a guitar more in the left speaker than the right. Which music technology process is this?
questions.solution: Panning places a sound between the left and right speakers in the stereo field
questions.hint: Think about the left–right position of a sound

feedback: Reverb adds the echoes of a room or hall
Quantising moves notes onto an exact rhythmic grid

questions.text: A producer adds an effect that makes a dry recording sound as if it was played in a large hall or church. Which effect is this?
questions.solution: Reverb (reverberation) adds the many reflections you hear in a large space
questions.hint: Think about the sound of singing in a big, echoing building

feedback: Distortion makes a sound gritty or fuzzy, as on a rock guitar

questions.text: A music file stores instructions such as which note to play, for how long and how loud, but no recorded sound. Give the abbreviation for this technology.
questions.solution: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) stores performance data, not audio
questions.hint: It is a four-letter abbreviation used to connect keyboards to computers

questions.text: An ensemble has two violins, a viola, a cello and a piano. What is it called?
questions.solution: Five players (a string quartet plus piano) make a piano quintet
questions.hint: Count the players first

feedback: A string quartet has no piano
A piano trio has only three players

questions.text: Which list of string instruments is in order from highest to lowest pitch range?
questions.solution: The smaller the string instrument, the higher it sounds: violin, viola, cello, double bass
questions.hint: Smaller instruments play higher

feedback: The violin is higher than the viola

questions.text: Which list contains only brass instruments?
questions.solution: Trumpet, French horn and tuba are all brass instruments
questions.hint: Check each list for any instrument that uses a reed

feedback: The saxophone is a woodwind instrument (it uses a reed)
The bassoon is woodwind
The clarinet is woodwind

questions.text: A producer moves notes that were played slightly out of time onto an exact rhythmic grid. What is this process called?
questions.solution: Quantising snaps notes to the nearest point on a rhythmic grid in a DAW
questions.hint: The process makes the timing exactly even

feedback: Sampling means recording and reusing a piece of sound

questions.text: In a symphony orchestra, which family usually sits at the front, nearest the conductor? Give the family.
questions.solution: The strings sit at the front, with woodwind behind, then brass and percussion at the back
questions.hint: It is the largest section of the orchestra

questions.text: Which instrument is the odd one out by family: flute, oboe, saxophone, horn?
questions.solution: The (French) horn is brass; the flute, oboe and saxophone are all woodwind
questions.hint: Be careful: some woodwind instruments are made of metal

feedback: The flute is woodwind even though it is made of metal
The saxophone is woodwind because it uses a reed

questions.text: A singer with a very high male voice sings in the alto range using falsetto. Give the name of this voice type.
questions.solution: A man who sings in the alto range is a countertenor
questions.hint: Its name includes the name of another male voice

feedback.tenor: The tenor is the highest common male voice, but lower than this

questions.text: Why is the saxophone classed as a woodwind instrument even though it is made of metal?
questions.solution: Instrument families depend on how the sound is made: the saxophone uses a reed, so it is woodwind
questions.hint: Families are decided by how the sound is made, not what the instrument is made of

options: A single reed vibrates against the mouthpiece to make the sound
The inventor was a woodwind player
The player buzzes their lips into a cup mouthpiece
Saxophones always sit with the woodwind in an orchestra
feedback: That is how brass instruments work

questions.text: Which statement about the timpani is accurate?
questions.solution: Timpani (kettledrums) are tuned percussion; the player changes the pitch with a pedal or tuning handles
questions.hint: They often play the tonic and dominant notes in an orchestra

options: They are untuned drums that cannot play definite pitches
They are tuned drums whose pitch can be changed, often with a pedal
They are a type of xylophone with wooden bars
They are played by plucking with the fingers
feedback: Timpani are tuned to definite notes

questions.text: Which marking would a composer write to make the violins sound muted and distant?
questions.solution: Con sordino means with a mute, which softens the string sound
questions.hint: Sordino is the Italian word for a mute

feedback: Fortissimo means very loud

questions.text: Which statement about how brass instruments make their sound is accurate?
questions.solution: Brass players buzz their lips; valves or a slide change the length of tube and so the pitch
questions.hint: Try making a sound by pressing your lips together and blowing

options: The player blows across an open hole
A reed vibrates against the mouthpiece
The player buzzes their lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece
feedback: That is how a flute works
That is woodwind

questions.text: Which instruments form the rhythm section of a jazz big band?
questions.solution: The rhythm section (piano, guitar, bass and drums) supplies the chords, bass line and beat
questions.hint: This section keeps the beat and plays the chords, not the horn melodies

options: Piano, guitar, double bass and drums
feedback: These are the horn sections that play the melodies and riffs

questions.text: A DAW lets a musician record, edit and mix audio on a computer. Give what the letters DAW stand for.
questions.solution: DAW stands for digital audio workstation
questions.hint: D is for digital

questions.text: Which composer belongs to the Baroque period?
questions.solution: J. S. Bach (1685–1750) is a Baroque composer; Bach's death in 1750 is often used to mark the end of the period
questions.hint: The Baroque period ended around 1750

feedback: Steve Reich is a minimalist composer
Chopin is a Romantic composer

questions.text: Which country does reggae music come from?
questions.solution: Reggae developed in Jamaica in the late 1960s; Bob Marley is its best-known star
questions.hint: Bob Marley was born there

feedback: Samba comes from Brazil
Calypso and steel pans come from Trinidad and Tobago

questions.text: Which country does samba come from?
questions.solution: Samba comes from Brazil and is famous at the Rio de Janeiro carnival
questions.hint: Think of the carnival in Rio de Janeiro

feedback: Argentina is famous for the tango

questions.text: Bhangra comes from which region of South Asia? Give the region.
questions.solution: Bhangra began as a harvest folk dance in the Punjab region, now split between India and Pakistan
questions.hint: The region's name means 'five rivers'

questions.text: Which composer is famous for minimalist music?
questions.solution: Steve Reich, with Philip Glass and Terry Riley, is a leading minimalist composer
questions.hint: Minimalism began in the USA in the 1960s

feedback: Mozart is a Classical-period composer
Handel is a Baroque composer

questions.text: Name the style of music that uses a 12-bar chord pattern and blue notes and began in African American communities in the southern USA.
questions.solution: The blues uses the 12-bar chord pattern and flattened 'blue' notes
questions.hint: The style is named after a colour linked with sadness

questions.text: Jazz singers sometimes improvise using nonsense syllables such as 'doo-bee-doo'. Give the term for this.
questions.solution: Scat singing uses nonsense syllables to improvise, as made famous by Louis Armstrong and Ella Fitzgerald
questions.hint: Ella Fitzgerald was famous for this style; the word is short

questions.text: Which instrument is most typical of Baroque music, often playing the continuo part?
questions.solution: The harpsichord often played the basso continuo in Baroque music
questions.hint: It is a keyboard instrument that plucks its strings

feedback: The saxophone was invented in the 1840s, long after the Baroque period

questions.text: Which feature is typical of minimalist music?
questions.solution: Minimalism uses short repeated cells (loops) that change gradually, by layering, phasing or adding notes
questions.hint: Think of loops that slowly change

options: Basso continuo played by a harpsichord
Short patterns repeated many times with gradual changes
Improvised scat singing over a swing rhythm
feedback: That is typical of Baroque music
That is typical of jazz

questions.text: In reggae, where do the guitar and keyboard usually play their short chords?
questions.solution: Reggae guitar and keyboard play short, choppy chords on the off-beats, called the skank
questions.hint: The chords avoid the strong beats

options: Only on the first beat of every bar
Long chords held for a whole bar
feedback: Reggae chords stress the off-beats, not beat 1

questions.text: In samba, what is the surdo?
questions.solution: The surdo is the deep bass drum that keeps the steady pulse of a samba band
questions.hint: It is the lowest-sounding instrument in the band

options: A small double bell played with a stick
A whistle used by the leader
A large bass drum that keeps the pulse
feedback: That is the agogo
That is the apito

questions.text: Name the large double-headed barrel drum, played with two sticks, that drives bhangra music.
questions.solution: The dhol is the double-headed barrel drum at the heart of bhangra
questions.hint: It is a four-letter word and is hung from the player's shoulder

questions.text: Which composer wrote music in the Classical period?
questions.solution: Mozart (1756–1791) is one of the main composers of the Classical period, with Haydn
questions.hint: The Classical period came after the Baroque

feedback: Bach is a Baroque composer
Vivaldi is a Baroque composer

questions.text: In a samba band, what is the apito?
questions.solution: The leader (mestre) blows the apito whistle to signal changes, breaks and endings
questions.hint: The leader needs to be heard above all the drums

options: A whistle the leader uses to give signals
A shaker made from a gourd

questions.text: A piece uses a harpsichord, basso continuo, terraced dynamics and many ornaments. Which period is it most likely from?
questions.solution: Harpsichord continuo, terraced dynamics and lots of ornaments are typical of Baroque music (about 1600–1750)
questions.hint: Which period used continuo throughout?

feedback: In the Classical period the piano replaced the harpsichord and crescendos became common

questions.text: A piece for a huge orchestra uses very wide dynamics, rubato and tells a story from a poem. Which period is it most likely from?
questions.solution: Large orchestras, extreme dynamics, rubato and programme music are typical of the Romantic period
questions.hint: Which period loved big emotions and stories in music?

feedback: Baroque orchestras were small and used terraced dynamics

questions.text: In a film, a short musical theme is linked to a character and returns whenever that character appears. What is it called?
questions.solution: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a character, place or idea, used by Wagner and in film music
questions.hint: The term was made famous by the opera composer Wagner

feedback: An ostinato is a pattern repeated continuously, not a theme linked to a character

questions.text: In film music, what is mickey-mousing?
questions.solution: Mickey-mousing closely matches music to actions, as in many cartoons
questions.hint: The name comes from cartoons

options: Music that the characters on screen can hear
Music that matches on-screen actions exactly, such as a slide for a fall
A slow love theme played on strings
Music played before the film starts
feedback: That is diegetic music

questions.text: In a film scene, the characters can hear a radio playing a song. Give the term for music that the characters themselves can hear.
questions.solution: Music that exists inside the story world, such as a radio in the scene, is diegetic
questions.hint: It comes from the Greek word for the story being told

feedback.non-diegetic: Non-diegetic music is added for the audience and the characters cannot hear it

questions.text: A jazz musician makes up a melody on the spot over the chords. Give the term for this.
questions.solution: Making up music on the spot is improvisation, a key feature of jazz
questions.hint: The music is not written down in advance

questions.text: In the 12-bar blues, which chord is played in bars 5 and 6?
questions.solution: The 12-bar blues is I I I I | IV IV I I | V IV I I, so bars 5 and 6 use chord IV
questions.hint: Write out the three lines of four bars and find the second line

feedback: Chord V first appears in bar 9

questions.text: A piece has a steady pulse and short repeated patterns that slowly drift out of time with each other. Which style and technique does this describe?
questions.solution: Patterns drifting out of sync is phase shifting (phasing), a minimalist technique used by Steve Reich
questions.hint: Think of two identical loops that gradually move apart

feedback: Rubato bends the tempo, but the pulse here stays steady

questions.text: Which feature would show that a piece is Classical rather than Baroque?
questions.solution: Balanced periodic phrases and the Alberti bass (broken-chord accompaniment) are typical of the Classical period
questions.hint: Look for the feature that the Baroque did not use

options: Balanced question-and-answer phrases with an Alberti bass accompaniment
A basso continuo played by harpsichord and cello
feedback: Continuo is a Baroque feature

questions.text: Which set of instruments is typical of traditional bhangra?
questions.solution: Traditional bhangra uses the dhol drum, the one-stringed tumbi and vocals
questions.hint: One of these is a large barrel drum played with two sticks

options: Steel pans, bass guitar and drum kit
feedback: Steel pans come from Trinidad
These are samba instruments

questions.text: Which statement about the basic 12-bar blues is accurate?
questions.solution: The basic 12-bar blues uses the three primary chords I, IV and V in a 12-bar pattern that repeats
questions.hint: Name the three primary chords

options: Only chords I and V are used, over 8 bars
The key must always be minor
Chords I, IV and V are used over 12 bars
feedback: Blues is often in a major key with flattened blue notes

questions.text: A style of music from Trinidad and Tobago uses tuned instruments made from oil drums. Give the name of these instruments.
questions.solution: Steel pans (steel drums) were developed in Trinidad and Tobago from oil drums
questions.hint: They are made from metal barrels and hit with sticks

questions.text: Which statement about blue notes is accurate?
questions.solution: Blue notes are flattened (or bent) notes, usually the 3rd, 5th and 7th, giving the blues its sound
questions.hint: They sound slightly lower than the notes of the major scale

options: They are sharpened notes, such as the 4th and 6th
They are notes played only by the trumpet
They are notes held for a whole bar
They are flattened notes, such as the 3rd and 7th of the scale
feedback: Blue notes are lowered, not raised

questions.text: Name the Jamaican singer-songwriter who led the Wailers and made reggae famous around the world.
questions.solution: Bob Marley (1945–1981) and the Wailers took reggae to a worldwide audience
questions.hint: His first name is a short form of Robert

questions.text: A Baroque bass line is played by a cello and a harpsichord, and the harpsichord player adds chords from figures written under the notes. What is this called?
questions.solution: The basso continuo was a bass line with figures showing the chords, played by a bass instrument and a keyboard
questions.hint: The part plays 'continuously' throughout the piece

feedback: Alberti bass is a Classical broken-chord pattern
Walking bass is a jazz bass line

questions.text: Why do Baroque pieces often change suddenly between loud and soft instead of using gradual crescendos?
questions.solution: Terraced dynamics suited instruments like the harpsichord and organ, which change volume in steps, not gradually
questions.hint: Think about the keyboard instruments used at the time

options: Composers were not allowed to write crescendos
Harpsichords and organs could not make gradual volume changes, so dynamics changed in blocks
feedback: Baroque orchestras were based on strings

questions.text: Which description fits a fugue?
questions.solution: A fugue is a polyphonic (contrapuntal) piece built on a subject that enters in each part in turn, as in Bach
questions.hint: J. S. Bach wrote many of these, each part entering in turn

options: A homophonic song with verses and a chorus
A slow piece with a single melody and no accompaniment
A polyphonic piece in which a subject is introduced by one part and then imitated by the other parts
A dance in triple time with a trio section
feedback: That describes a minuet and trio

questions.text: Why did the piano gradually replace the harpsichord in the Classical period?
questions.solution: The pianoforte ('soft-loud') could make gradual dynamic changes, which suited Classical style
questions.hint: Its full name, pianoforte, gives a clue

options: The piano had no strings, so it was louder
Only the piano could play more than one note at a time
The piano could play softer or louder depending on how hard the keys were pressed
feedback: Harpsichords can also play chords

questions.text: In reggae, the bass drum and snare often hit together on beat 3 of the bar instead of beat 1. Give the name of this drum pattern.
questions.solution: The one drop pattern stresses beat 3 and leaves beat 1 empty
questions.hint: Beat 1 is 'dropped'

questions.text: Which statement about British bhangra is accurate?
questions.solution: British bhangra, developed by the Punjabi community in the UK, fuses folk bhangra with Western pop and dance styles
questions.hint: It is a fusion style made by a community living in Britain

options: Traditional Punjabi music is mixed with Western pop, dance or hip hop styles
A form of Baroque church music
A style that began in Brazil for carnival processions
feedback: That describes samba

questions.text: Which statement about Romantic music is accurate?
questions.solution: Romantic composers wrote programme music and used larger orchestras with a wide range of dynamics
questions.hint: Think about stories, emotions and big orchestras

options: Composers mostly used the harpsichord with a basso continuo
Composers often wrote programme music that tells a story or describes a scene
Orchestras became smaller than in the Classical period
feedback: Romantic orchestras grew larger
